title: Scalar extension of each line is the target line, with the specified map.
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E,L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with a specified $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra embedding $\iota:E\to L$, and let $S$ be any scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $F=E,L$ put $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,S}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n)_S$, with the constant and completed scalar maps of [def-pur-twist-coefficient-rings]. Let $\alpha:R_E\to R_L$ be the map characterized by the maps induced by $\iota$ on all these finite quotients. Let $Z=\mathrm{purTwistZlModule}(S,\ell)$ and $T_F(1)=\mathrm{purTwistIntegralModule}(S,\ell,F)$ be the root-limit module and its integral coefficient tensor, with the specified completed actions [def-pur-twist-sheaves]. Define $T_F(0)=R_F$, $T_F(r)=T_F(1)^{\otimes_{R_F}r}$ for $r\geq1$ and $T_F(-r)=\mathcal Hom_{R_F}(T_F(r),R_F)$ for $r\geq1$, using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. These are the module sheaves denoted integralTwistLine in the attached Lean declaration.

Let $c_m:T_E(m)\to\operatorname{Res}_\alpha T_L(m)$, with $\operatorname{Res}_\alpha$ restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], be the unique normalized semilinear family of [lem-route-twist-scalar-maps-exists-unique]. Explicitly, $c_0=\alpha$; $c_1(b\otimes z)=\iota(b)\otimes z$ for sections $b$ of the discrete constant integer sheaf and $z$ of $Z$; $c_{r+1}(x\otimes y)=c_r(x)\otimes c_1(y)$ for $r\geq1$; and $c_{-r}(\varphi)(c_r(x))=\alpha(\varphi(x))$ for $r\geq1$, on every localized site. Here $\iota(b)$ denotes the map on the constant integer sheaves induced by $\iota$, and tensor sections mean their images under sheafification.

Write $F_\alpha(M)=R_L\otimes_{R_E}M$ for ordinary sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $[s\otimes x]_U$ for the sheafification-unit section [def-sp-scalar-tensor-comparison-data]. Thus $F_\alpha$ and these sections are integralOrdinaryScalar and integralOrdinaryTensorSection, including their specified object-equality transports. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$ there is exactly one isomorphism of $R_L$-module sheaves
$$B_m:F_\alpha(T_E(m))\xrightarrow{\sim}T_L(m)$$
such that for every site object $U$, $s\in R_L(U)$ and $x\in T_E(m)(U)$,
$$ (B_m)_U([s\otimes x]_U)=s\,c_{m,U}(x). $$

source.place: lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar: the Lean of this node (its declaration uses) reaches WeilConjectures.twistLineScalarIso_existsUnique, a sorry on the sorry route of batch5 with no node; Lean: SHEAF file lean/Sheaf/Paper/CoefficientTwistsDetailed.lean, declaration WeilConjectures.twistLineScalarIso_existsUnique (module Sheaf.Paper.CoefficientTwistsDetailed, lines 509-524, proof `sorry`)

proof.text: Use the existence assertion of [lem-route-twist-scalar-maps-exists-unique] to fix its normalized family $c$. The ordinary scalar adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction] applies to $\alpha$ and the actual ordinary tensor functor. Transpose $c_1$ to an $R_L$-linear morphism $b:F_\alpha(T_E(1))\to T_L(1)$. Its unit formula gives $b([1\otimes x])=c_1(x)$, hence $b([s\otimes x])=s c_1(x)$ by linearity. The hypotheses here are module sheafification on the small pro-etale site and the ring-sheaf map $\alpha$; no derived or constructibility hypothesis is being invoked.

source.place: Integral signed twists and scalar extension; worker assembly step 1. Stacks 03EK (section-tensor-product), 04TT (section-internal-hom), 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom); specified normalization in CoefficientTwistsDetailed.lean, ScalarComparison.

proof.text: Choose a covering of the final site object trivializing $Z$ by [lem-pur-twist-root-local-models]. On a member $V$ let $e$ be the image of $1$ under this trivialization, and put $e_F=[1\otimes e]\in T_F(1)(V)$ for $F=E,L$. These are bases over the completed rings, not merely over the discrete constant rings: by [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction], the defining discrete coefficient tensor can be computed on the localized site; after replacing $Z|_V$ by $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell}|_V$, its coefficient map is exactly $b\otimes r\mapsto d_F(b)c_F(r)$. This is bijective on each object by [lem-pur-twist-coefficient-tensor]. The action characterized in [lem-pur-tensor-pushout-action] makes this identification $R_F$-linear: multiplication by $d_F(b)$ is the original constant coefficient action, and multiplication by $c_F(r)$ sends $b'\otimes e$ to $b'\otimes r e$. Consequently $r\mapsto r e_F$ identifies $R_F|_V$ with $T_F(1)|_V$. The sectionwise coefficient inverses respect restrictions because their forward maps do, and therefore give inverse sheaf maps. The same cover works for both fields.

source.place: Integral signed twists and scalar extension; worker assembly step 2. Stacks 03EK (section-tensor-product), 04TT (section-internal-hom), 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom); specified normalization in CoefficientTwistsDetailed.lean, ScalarComparison.

proof.text: The exponent-one normalization of $c$ gives $c_1(e_E)=e_L$, since the map on constant integer sheaves preserves $1$. Semilinearity gives $c_1(r e_E)=\alpha(r)e_L$. Thus, in the bases from step 2, $b|_V$ and the multiplication below agree on all local tensors $[s\otimes re_E]$, so by the tensor extensionality of [lem-weil-ramified-finite-tensor-sections] (applied on the localized site to the actual sheaf tensor) $b|_V$ is the sheaf tensor multiplication $R_L\otimes_{R_E}R_E\to R_L$, $s\otimes r\mapsto s\alpha(r)$. The normalized unit comparison of [def-sp-canonical-scalar-extension-maps] is exactly this isomorphism, with inverse $z\mapsto[z\otimes1]$. Localized tensor restriction [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] identifies its source with the restriction of the global source of $b$. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] to the underlying abelian sheaves: the cover of the final object covers every object by pullback, and each restricted morphism is invertible. The resulting inverse is $R_L$-linear, since $b^{-1}(a y)=a b^{-1}(y)$ follows by applying the injective linear map $b$. Hence $b$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves.

source.place: Integral signed twists and scalar extension; worker assembly step 3. Stacks 03EK (section-tensor-product), 04TT (section-internal-hom), 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom); specified normalization in CoefficientTwistsDetailed.lean, ScalarComparison.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-signed-line-scalar-tensor-tower] to $R_0=R_E$, $R_1=R_2=R_L$, lines $T_E(1),T_L(1),T_L(1)$ and comparisons $b_{01}=b_{02}=b$ and $b_{12}$ the scalar unit. The required initial tower equation is the unit identity: both composites send $(s\otimes x)\otimes t$ to $st c_1(x)$. Both lines are locally units by step 2, and the small pro-etale site has finite limits and final object. The lemma supplies isomorphisms $B_m:F_\alpha(T_E(m))\cong T_L(m)$ for all integers. Their degree-zero map is multiplication, degree-one map is $b$, positive maps obey the tensor recursion, and for $r>0$ their negative and positive maps satisfy
$$\operatorname{ev}(B_{-r}([s\otimes\varphi]),B_r([t\otimes x]))=st\alpha(\varphi(x)).$$
The lemma uses right scalar tensors; use the scalar-first convention by interchanging the written positions of the two factors. Its displayed formulas already specify the resulting maps on these generators.

source.place: Integral signed twists and scalar extension; worker assembly step 4. Stacks 03EK (section-tensor-product), 04TT (section-internal-hom), 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom); specified normalization in CoefficientTwistsDetailed.lean, ScalarComparison.

proof.text: Define $d_m(x)=B_m([1\otimes x])$. The scalar adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction] makes $d_m$ a morphism into restriction of scalars, so these maps are semilinear and natural on all slices. The four normalizations are now explicit: $d_0(r)=\alpha(r)$ by the scalar unit; $d_1=c_1$ by step 1; $d_{r+1}(x\otimes y)=d_r(x)\otimes d_1(y)$ by positive recursion; and $d_{-r}(\varphi)(d_r(x))=\alpha(\varphi(x))$ by the evaluation formula in step 4 with $s=t=1$. Thus $d$ satisfies the exact predicate IsCanonicalTwistScalarMaps, not just a local rank-one condition. Uniqueness in [lem-route-twist-scalar-maps-exists-unique] gives $d=c$. Finally $R_L$-linearity gives $B_m([s\otimes x])=s B_m([1\otimes x])=s c_m(x)$, which proves existence with the requested formula for every $m$, including zero and negative exponents.

source.place: Integral signed twists and scalar extension; worker assembly step 5. Stacks 03EK (section-tensor-product), 04TT (section-internal-hom), 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom); specified normalization in CoefficientTwistsDetailed.lean, ScalarComparison.

proof.text: If $B'_m$ is another isomorphism with the formula, its forward morphism and that of $B_m$ agree on every $[1\otimes x]$. The ordinary tensor extensionality statement of [lem-weil-ramified-finite-tensor-sections], applied to the actual sheafified scalar-extension presentation, gives equality of their forward morphisms. Their inverses are equal as well: if $f$ is this common forward morphism and $g,h$ are the inverses, then $g=g(fh)=(gf)h=h$. This proves the asserted unique existence. On the empty scheme the covering and sheaf arguments still apply and all section equalities hold in zero modules; no argument required a nonzero basis section.

theorem twistLineScalarIso_existsUnique (m : ℤ) :
    ∃! c : (integralOrdinaryScalar ℓ E L ι S).obj (integralTwistLine ℓ E S m) ≅
        integralTwistLine ℓ L S m,
      ∀ (U : S.ProEtᵒᵖ) (s : (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted ℓ L S).obj.obj U)
        (x : (integralTwistLine ℓ E S m).val.obj U),
        c.hom.val.app U
            (integralOrdinaryTensorSection ℓ E L ι S _ U s x) =
          s • (@id ((integralTwistLine ℓ L S m).val.obj U)
            ((twistScalarMaps ℓ E S L ι m).val.app U x)) := by
  sorry
